legend: You are probably familiar with the classic problem of finding the longest increasing subsequence in an array. Let a%%ZSMJ0%% be an array consisting of n%%ZSMJ1%% integers. A subsequence i1<i2<…<ik%%ZSMJ2%% is called increasing if ai1<ai2<…<aik%%ZSMJ3%%. The longest increasing subsequence is the increasing subsequence of maximum length. Of course, we will not ask you to solve the classic problem; you will have to solve its more complicated version...

Initially, there is an empty array a%%ZSMJ4%%. Then, the numbers 1,2,…,n%%ZSMJ5%% are added to the array in this order. The number i%%ZSMJ6%% is added to the array at position pi%%ZSMJ7%%. Positions in the array are numbered with integers from 1%%ZSMJ8%% to k%%ZSMJ9%%, where k%%ZSMJ10%% is the current size of the array. When adding an element at position p%%ZSMJ11%% in an array of size k%%ZSMJ12%%, all elements that previously had positions from p%%ZSMJ13%% to k%%ZSMJ14%% are shifted one position to the right, and the current element is added to the freed space.
Your task is to determine the length of the longest increasing subsequence in the array after each addition of a new element.
input: The first line contains one integer n%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤n≤200000%%ZSMJ16%%) — the number of added elements.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ17%% integers p1,p2,…,pn%%ZSMJ18%% (1≤pi≤i%%ZSMJ19%%) — pi%%ZSMJ20%% denotes the position where element i%%ZSMJ21%% is added.
output: Output n%%ZSMJ22%% integers — the length of the longest increasing subsequence of the array after each addition of a new element.
note: The array in the first example changed as follows: []→[1]→[1,2]→[3,1,2]→[3,1,4,2]→[3,1,4,5,2]%%ZSMJ23%%.
